Package neqsim.thermo

Class ThermodynamicModelTest

java.lang.Object
neqsim.thermo.ThermodynamicModelTest
All Implemented Interfaces:
Serializable, ThermodynamicConstantsInterface
public class ThermodynamicModelTest extends Object implements ThermodynamicConstantsInterface
Checks thermodynamic identities and the declared derivatives of logarithmic fugacity coefficients.

    • checkNumerically

      public boolean checkNumerically()
      Compares declared T, P and mole derivatives with independent finite differences on detached snapshots.

      Each active logical phase is checked on its retained root without flashing or mutating the supplied fluid. Two second-order estimates, at a step and half that step, must agree with each other and with the analytic derivative. Their tolerance is maxError * max(1, abs(analytic), abs(numerical)); callers must choose an accuracy that their property evaluator and finite differences can resolve. An unresolved or non-finite check returns false. Mole perturbations never remove more than the available amount; boundary components use a one-sided stencil. These are the unconstrained partial derivatives exposed by the component API. Electrolyte model qualification also requires separate charge-preserving directional checks and is not established by this method alone.

      Returns:
      true only when every derivative and its step-size consistency check meets the configured tolerance

    • differences

      private double[] differences(byte[] snapshot, int phase, int variable, double step, boolean central)
      Computes all logarithmic fugacity derivatives for one coordinate using an independent second-order stencil.
      Parameters:
      snapshot - serialized initialized reference state
      phase - logical phase index
      variable - minus two for T, minus one for P, otherwise component mole index
      step - positive finite perturbation
      central - whether the negative perturbation remains inside the physical amount domain
      Returns:
      numerical derivatives for all components in the phase
